title: Parallel Courses
summary: Take any number of courses per semester once their prerequisites are done; find the fewest semesters needed, or -1.

tests.explain: Semester 1: course 1. Semester 2: courses 2 and 3, which both only needed 1. Semester 3: course 4, which needed 3.
1 → 2 → 3 → 1 is a loop, so none of these courses can ever be started: -1.
Nothing depends on anything, so all five courses fit in one semester.

hints: In the first semester you can take every course with no prerequisites. Which courses become available for the second semester?
Run Kahn's algorithm one level at a time: the current level is everything with in-degree 0 right now. Taking all of them unlocks the next level. Count the levels.
Courses are numbered 1 to n, so size your arrays n + 1. If fewer than n courses were ever taken, a cycle blocks the rest: return -1.

complexity.time: O(n + E): every course and relation is processed once
complexity.space: O(n + E): the adjacency list, in-degrees and the current level
